conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by The McNay in 2025.
conservation.technical_description:
The work is executed with low impasto throughout; due to the sheer application of primer and paint, the darkness of the canvas is apparent. Several canvas imperfections are perceptible through the paint. Slubs are located as follows: one is 6 in. from the top and 6 in. from the right and ½ in. long.  Another is 13 in. from the top, 13 in. from the right edge and ¾ in. long.  A third is 7 ½ in. from the top, 2 ½ in. from the left edge and ½ in. long.  And the final slub is located 2 in. from the top, 6 ½ in. from the left and is 1 in. long.  Several spot imperfections are located in the lower left corner.  One is 2 in. from the bottom and 1 ¼ in. from the left.  Another is 4 in. form the bottom and 1 ¼ in. from the left.  A third is 11 ½ from the bottom edge and 6 ½ in. from the left. 
 
Several areas of the painting contain splatters of unknown origins. These areas are located in the upper right corner, around the center of the pink hollyhock, and below the center of the yellow hollyhock.

remarks_1999: Abiquiú Notebooks indicates in 1955 Atlanta exhibition "though not listed in catalogue." Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 indicates, "Sold by Halpert to Jones — Feb. 1959." O'Keeffe wrote: "There is a pink and yellow hollyhock but it isn't a show painting" (O'Keeffe to Edith Halpert, 8 August 1954, Archive of American Art). See cat. no. 1979. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: Collection of the McNay Art Museum, Bequest of Helen Miller Jones (1989.37)
description: A pink hollyhock hovers at the top of the composition, while a yellow bloom fills the lower half of the canvas. The flowers have protruding white centers and sit against a plain yellow and green background.
title: Pink and Yellow Hollyhocks
